problem.text: An infinite sequence of real numbers $a_1, a_2, \dots$ satisfies the recurrence $a_{n+3} = a_{n+2} - 2a_{n+1} + a_n$ for every positive integer $n$. Given that $a_1 = a_3 = 1$ and $a_{98} = a_{99}$, compute $a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{100}$.

steps.title: Where to start: add up the recurrence itself
steps.body: We do not know $a_2$, so we cannot compute the terms one by one. But we want a sum, and the coefficients on the right side, $1$, $-2$ and $1$, add up to $0$. That is the clue: if we add many copies of the recurrence, most terms should cancel.

your_turn.prompt: Write the recurrence for $n = 1$ and for $n = 2$.

steps.title: Add the equations for $n = 1$ to $n = 97$
steps.body: The equation for $n = 97$ has $a_{100}$ on the left, so we add the $97$ equations for $n = 1, 2, \dots, 97$. The left sides add up to $a_4 + a_5 + \cdots + a_{100}$. The right side is (the sum of all the $a_{n+2}$) minus $2$ times (the sum of all the $a_{n+1}$) plus (the sum of all the $a_n$).

your_turn.prompt: As $n$ runs from $1$ to $97$, which terms make up each of those three sums?
your_turn.answer: $a_{n+2}$ runs over $a_3, \dots, a_{99}$; $a_{n+1}$ over $a_2, \dots, a_{98}$; and $a_n$ over $a_1, \dots, a_{97}$.

steps.title: Count what survives on the right
steps.body: Any term from $a_4$ to $a_{97}$ is in all three sums, so its total coefficient is $1 - 2 + 1 = 0$ and it cancels. The term $a_1$ is only in the last sum (coefficient $+1$), and $a_{99}$ is only in the first sum (coefficient $+1$). So only $a_1$, $a_2$, $a_3$, $a_{98}$ and $a_{99}$ can remain.

your_turn.prompt: Find the total coefficients of $a_2$, $a_3$ and $a_{98}$ on the right side.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
We now have $a_4 + \cdots + a_{100} = a_1 - a_2 + a_{99} - a_{98}$. Add $a_1 + a_2 + a_3$ to both sides; the unknown $a_2$ cancels:
$$a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{100} = 2a_1 + a_3 + (a_{99} - a_{98})$$
With $a_1 = a_3 = 1$ and $a_{98} = a_{99}$, this is $2 + 1 + 0 = 3$. The answer is **$3$**.
